title: The Bridge
author: Alexandre Dias
contentWarnings: Themes of exhaustion and voluntary withdrawal
excerpt: The bridge was not on the map. Aoife had, on the fourth evening of her walking holiday on the west coast of Ireland, taken a small wrong turn onto an unmarked lane. It had led her, in ten minutes of walking in the failing light, to a small wooden bridge over a small stream. She had, at the bridge, felt the specific small feeling of an invitation. She had walked across.

chapters.title: Invitation
chapters.body:
The bridge was not on the map.

Aoife Callaghan was thirty-three, and she had, in the second week of September, come to a small village on the west coast of Ireland for a two-week walking holiday that she had, in the specific small careful way of a woman who had over-planned it, arranged for herself as a small reward for the completion of a small careful project at her small firm in Dublin. She had booked a small cottage in the village of Louisburgh. She had brought with her a small careful walking stick and a small careful pair of boots and a small careful set of maps of the small careful area, and she had, on her first three days in the cottage, done the small careful walks the small careful area was known for — up the small mountain, along the small cliffs, out to the small ruined chapel on the small rocky headland.

On the fourth evening she had, after her small careful dinner at the small careful pub in the village, walked back to the small cottage in the small pale September twilight, and had, on the small road just outside the village, taken a small wrong turn.

She had not, at the time, understood that it was a wrong turn. She had turned onto a small unmarked lane that had, in the small pale light, seemed to run in the direction she wanted to go. She had walked along it for perhaps ten minutes. The small lane had, over the ten minutes, become smaller — had narrowed from a small paved road to a small gravel track to a small dirt path — and had, at the end of the ten minutes, come to a small wooden bridge over a small stream.

She had, at the small wooden bridge, stopped.

The small bridge had been perhaps six meters long. It had been made of small dark wooden planks, weathered in the specific small way of wood that had been out in the Atlantic weather for a great many years. It had had small handrails on either side, of the same small dark wood. It had crossed a small stream that had been perhaps two meters below.

She had, at the small bridge, been aware of the specific small feeling of not, at that moment, being where she thought she was.

She had, in the specific small careful way of a woman doing a small careful check, taken out her phone. She had, at the small phone, tried to open the small map application. The small map application had, at the small tap, failed to load. The small phone had, at the small check, shown no signal.

She had, in the specific small careful way, put the phone away.

She had considered turning back.

She had understood, considering it, that the small careful thing to do was to turn back. She had walked, on unfamiliar ground, for ten minutes in the small failing light. She had lost her small signal. She had, so far as she could see, no small careful reason to cross the small bridge.

She had, all the same, walked forward.

She had done this in the specific small careful way of a woman who had, over the last three days of her small careful walking holiday, become, in some small quiet way, curious. She had done it because the small bridge had had, at the specific small moment of her arriving at it, the specific small quiet quality of a small careful invitation. It had been, in the small dim light, waiting.

She had walked onto the small bridge.

She had walked across it. The small wooden planks had, under her small careful boots, made a small careful sound. The small stream below her had, in the small quiet, made a small careful sound of its own. She had, at the small other side of the small bridge, stepped off onto a small careful path that continued into a small dark stand of small careful trees.

She had turned around.

She had, in the specific small careful way, wanted to check the small bridge from the other side.

The small bridge had not been there.

The small careful trees on the far side had, in the specific small careful way, closed. The small path she had just walked along had, in the specific small careful way, ended. The small stream had gone on running, in the specific small careful way of a small stream, but there had been no small bridge crossing it. There had been, at the small point where the small bridge had been, only the small dark water and the small careful bank on either side.

Aoife had, at the small point, been very still.

She had, in the specific small careful way of a woman not entirely permitting herself to run, walked back to the small edge of the small stream. She had looked at the small water. The small water had been perhaps two meters below the small bank, in the specific small dark quiet way of a small Irish stream in September. She had looked at the small other side. The small other side had been perhaps six meters away.

She had, in the specific small careful way, understood that she was not going to be able to jump.

She had understood, further, that the small bridge had, in the specific small careful way, been an invitation.

She had understood, at last, that she had, in the specific small careful way, accepted.

chapters.title: The Cottage
chapters.body:
She had walked into the small stand of trees.

She had done this in the specific small careful way of a woman who had understood that the small careful thing to do was to see where she was, and that the small small failing light was not, at the small moment, going to give her many more small options. She had followed the small path.

The small path had, over the following perhaps fifteen minutes, led her through a small stand of trees that had, on her careful attention, been somewhat older than the small trees she had, over the last three days, seen in the small careful area — small oaks and small ashes of a small careful maturity that suggested a small careful wood that had not, in the recent past, been managed. She had emerged, at the end of the small path, into a small clearing.

The small clearing had held a small house.

The small house had been a small stone cottage of the specific small careful sort that the small careful area was, in the specific small careful way, known for. It had had a small careful roof of small careful thatch. It had had small careful whitewashed walls. It had had, on the small careful front, a small careful red door and two small careful windows through which small careful yellow light had been coming.

Aoife had, at the edge of the small clearing, stopped.

She had, for a long moment, considered.

She had considered that the small house, in the specific small careful way, appeared to be inhabited. She had considered that it was, in the specific small failing light, nearly full dark. She had considered that she had, in the specific small careful way, no small other option — the small bridge was gone, the small path she had come along had, on her careful look back, closed in behind her, and the small light was going.

She had walked forward.

She had, at the small red door, hesitated for a moment. She had, at last, knocked.

The small door had, after a small moment, been opened by a small old woman.

The small old woman had been perhaps eighty. She had had small careful white hair pinned in a small careful way at the small back of her small careful head. She had been wearing a small careful grey dress of the specific small careful sort her grandmother, Aoife thought, might have worn. She had, on seeing Aoife, made a small careful small sound of specific small warm surprise.

She had said, in Irish, in a small careful voice: *ah. Ah, you have come. Come in, child. Come in.*

Aoife had, at the small door, said: *I am — I am sorry to bother you. I got a little lost. I —*

The small old woman had said: *of course you did. Come in. It is nearly dark.*

Aoife had, in the specific small careful way of a woman not entirely sure what she was doing, gone in.

The small inside of the small cottage had been the specific small warm inside of a small careful traditional Irish cottage. A small careful fire had been burning in a small careful hearth. A small careful kettle had been on a small careful hook over the small careful fire. There had been a small careful wooden table with two small careful wooden chairs. The small old woman had, in the specific small careful way of a small old Irish woman, gestured to one of the small chairs.

Aoife had sat.

The small old woman had, in the specific small careful way, taken the small careful kettle from the small careful hook, and had, at a small careful counter, poured a small careful cup of tea. She had brought the small tea to Aoife. She had, at Aoife's small chair, sat down on the other small chair.

She had said: *I have been waiting for you.*

Aoife had said: *for me?*

The small old woman had said: *for one of you.*

Aoife had said: *what — what do you mean.*

The small old woman had said, in the specific small careful way of a small woman who had said this before: *the small bridge appears, child, for those it is willing to have. It does not appear every night. It appears when it wishes to. And when it appears, it is because — it is because there is someone in the small world outside who has, at that specific small moment, needed to cross it. The small bridge chooses. You crossed. That means you were, at the moment of walking down the small lane, someone who needed to cross.*

Aoife had said, quietly: *needed to cross to where.*

The small old woman had said: *to here.*

Aoife had said: *and where is here.*

The small old woman had, at this, been quiet for a moment.

She had said, at last: *here is — here is the small place where certain small careful people go when they have, in their small careful lives, come to a small careful moment where they need to sit down. It is not, child, a place you can find on a map. It is not a place that is, in the specific small careful way, in any specific small location. It is a small careful place that appears, in the small careful way of the small bridge, when the small careful need is there.*

Aoife had said: *and you.*

The small old woman had said: *I am the small careful woman who has, for perhaps ninety years now, lived in the small cottage.*

Aoife had said: *ninety.*

The small old woman had said, in her small careful way: *I was, in what you would call the ordinary world, a small careful young woman on the small careful island of Achill in nineteen and thirty-four. I was, at that time, seventeen. I had, at that time, been in a small careful trouble. I do not — I do not remember, exactly, what the small trouble was. But I had, in the small careful late evening, walked out of my small careful house and had, in the small careful way, walked down a small lane that had had, at the end of it, a small careful wooden bridge. I had crossed the small bridge. I had come to the small cottage. The small careful woman who had been in the small cottage at that time had — had let me in. Had given me tea. Had let me sit.*

*I had, over the small following weeks, understood a small thing.*

*I had understood that the small careful woman who had, before me, lived in the small cottage was, in the specific small careful way, tired. She had, in the specific small careful way, been in the small cottage for a small long time. She had been waiting for someone to come who would, in the specific small careful way, take her small place.*

*I had, at seventeen, taken her small place.*

*She had gone, in the specific small careful way, out through the small back door of the small cottage. I do not — I do not know where she went. I have never, in the ninety years since, gone through the small back door myself. I have only, in the small careful way, kept the small cottage. I have made the small tea. I have waited for the small careful next person.*

*You, child, are the small careful next person.*

Aoife had, at the small careful table, put down the small careful cup.

She had said, in a small careful voice: *no.*

The small old woman had said: *no?*

Aoife had said: *I do not — I have not — I do not have a small careful trouble that has driven me out onto a small lane. I have, at this small careful moment in my life, a small careful job I like and a small careful flat in Dublin and a small careful sister I love and small careful parents who are, in the specific small careful way, alive and small careful friends and — I have, in the specific small careful way, everything. I do not need to sit down.*

The small old woman had, at this, looked at Aoife for a long moment.

The small old woman had said, quietly: *and yet you crossed the small bridge.*

Aoife had said: *I did.*

The small old woman had said: *why.*

Aoife had, at the small careful question, been quiet for a moment.

She had said, at last, more quietly: *because it was there.*

The small old woman had said: *that is not, in the specific small careful way, why.*

Aoife had said, more quietly still: *because I was — I was, in the small careful way, curious.*

The small old woman had said: *and.*

Aoife had, at the small careful table, been quiet for a longer moment.

She had said, at last: *because I have, in the small careful way, been tired for some time.*

The small old woman had said, in the specific small careful way of a woman who had been quietly waiting for this specific small sentence: *ah.*

Aoife had said: *I did not — I did not know I was tired. But I have, since — since coming to the small careful village three days ago, understood that I have been tired for a very long time. I have been, in my small careful Dublin life, doing the small careful things a small careful woman of thirty-three does, and I have been, in the specific small careful way, tired by all of them. I did not know. I did not, at any point, admit to myself. But the small careful bridge — the small careful bridge knew.*

The small old woman had said: *the small careful bridge knew.*

Aoife had said, quietly: *and it brought me here.*

The small old woman had said: *it brought you here.*

chapters.title: The Back Door
chapters.body:
She had, that night, slept in the small cottage.

She had done this in the specific small careful way of a woman who had, over the small careful evening's conversation, understood two things.

She had understood, first, that the small old woman was, in the specific small careful way, telling her the small careful truth. That the small cottage was, in the small careful way, a small careful place of small careful rest. That the small old woman had been there for ninety years, waiting for someone to come who would, in the specific small careful way, take her small place. That the small small careful path back to the small ordinary world would, in some small careful way, be shown to her if she wanted it.

She had understood, second, that she was not, in the specific small careful way, going to take it.

She had understood this in the small careful way one understood such small careful things — not by any small careful thinking, but by a small careful settling in her small careful body. She had, over the small evening, felt the small careful warm quiet of the small cottage settle into her small careful bones. She had felt the small careful weight of the small careful last five years of her small careful Dublin life — the small careful long hours, the small careful ambition, the small careful small careful attention she had, over the years, paid to every small careful small thing — begin to lift.

She had, in the specific small careful way, understood that she had, at thirty-three, been in the small careful way, more tired than she had ever, in her small careful life, permitted herself to know.

She had, at the small careful hour of eleven, said to the small old woman, quietly: *I would like to stay.*

The small old woman had said: *I know, child.*

Aoife had said: *and you — you will go.*

The small old woman had said: *tomorrow. Tomorrow, when you have slept.*

Aoife had said: *where will you go.*

The small old woman had said, quietly: *I do not know. I have not — I have not, in ninety years, permitted myself to think about it. It has been a small careful gift, that I did not have to think about it. But now — now, at last, I am permitted.*

She had, at this, been quiet for a moment.

She had said, more quietly: *I think I will go and find my sister.*

Aoife had said: *your sister?*

The small old woman had said: *she died — she died in the small careful year before I came to the small bridge. I have — I have missed her. I have missed her for ninety years. I have thought, over the small careful ninety years, that when I was, at last, permitted to go — I would go to find her.*

Aoife had said, quietly: *I hope you find her.*

The small old woman had said: *I hope so too.*

—

Aoife had slept, that night, in the small careful cot at the small back of the small cottage.

She had slept the specific small careful deep sleep she had not, in perhaps ten years, slept.

She had, in the morning, woken to the small careful sound of the small careful old woman at the small careful fire.

The small old woman had, when Aoife had risen, made her a small careful breakfast of small careful bread and small careful butter and small careful tea. They had eaten it together at the small careful table. They had, over the small careful breakfast, spoken quietly of small careful things — of the small careful garden behind the small cottage, of the small careful herbs the small old woman had, over the ninety years, grown in it, of the small careful way one kept the small careful fire, of the small careful way one greeted the small careful next small careful visitor when they came.

The small old woman had said: *she will come, child. Perhaps in a year. Perhaps in ten. Perhaps in fifty. The small careful bridge will send her when she is ready.*

Aoife had said: *and I will wait.*

The small old woman had said: *you will wait.*

Aoife had said: *what will I do, in the meantime.*

The small old woman had, at this, smiled.

She had said, quietly: *the small careful garden. The small careful cottage. The small careful small careful things a small careful woman does when she has, in the specific small careful way, at last been permitted to stop.*

Aoife had said: *and I will not — I will not be lonely.*

The small old woman had said, in the specific small careful way: *you will be, child. You will be. But you will find, over the small careful years, that the small careful loneliness of the small careful cottage is a small careful different loneliness than the small careful loneliness of the small careful outside. It is — it is the small careful loneliness of a small careful woman who has, in the specific small careful way, chosen to be alone. Not the small careful loneliness of a small careful woman who has, in the small careful way, not chosen anything.*

*You will find, in the small careful way, that the small careful chosen loneliness is small careful bearable.*

Aoife had said, quietly: *I believe you.*

The small old woman had, at the small careful table, at the small careful end of the small careful breakfast, taken Aoife's small careful hand.

She had said: *thank you, child.*

Aoife had said: *thank you.*

The small old woman had gotten up. She had, in the specific small careful way, walked to the small back door of the small cottage. She had, at the small back door, put her hand on the small careful handle. She had, for a small careful moment, looked back at Aoife.

She had said: *tell the small careful next one — when she comes — that I said the small careful loneliness is small careful bearable.*

Aoife had said: *I will.*

The small old woman had opened the small back door.

Aoife had not, in the specific small careful way, been able to see what had been on the small other side of the small back door. She had seen only a small careful bright pale light. The small old woman had, in the specific small careful way, walked into the small careful bright pale light. The small back door had, in the specific small careful way, closed.

Aoife had, at the small careful table, been alone in the small cottage.

—

She had lived in the small cottage for the small careful rest of her life.

She had, in the specific small careful way, kept the small careful garden. She had kept the small careful fire. She had made the small careful tea. She had waited for the small careful next visitor.

The small careful next visitor had come, at last, on a small careful evening in October, forty-seven years later.

The small careful next visitor had been a small careful young woman of about twenty-nine, who had, in the specific small careful way, been walking on a small careful lane on the small careful west coast of Ireland in the small careful failing light. She had come to the small careful bridge. She had, in the specific small careful way, crossed it. She had come to the small cottage.

Aoife had, at the small careful red door, opened it.

She had said, in her own small careful old voice: *ah. Ah, you have come. Come in, child. Come in.*

The small careful young woman had, in the specific small careful way, come in.

Aoife had made her a small careful cup of tea.

Aoife had, in the specific small careful way, told her the small careful story.

Aoife had, at the small careful end of the small careful story, added the small careful thing the small old woman had, forty-seven years earlier, told her to add.

Aoife had said, quietly: *the small careful woman before me told me to tell you: the small careful loneliness is small careful bearable.*

The small careful young woman had said: *I understand.*

They had, at the small careful table, sat with the small careful tea.

The small careful next morning, Aoife had, in the specific small careful way, walked to the small back door of the small cottage.

She had, at the small back door, put her hand on the small careful handle. She had, for a small careful moment, looked back at the small careful next woman.

She had said: *tell her — tell her, when she comes, that the small careful loneliness is small careful bearable.*

The small careful next woman had said: *I will.*

Aoife had opened the small back door.

She had walked into the small careful bright pale light.

She had, in the specific small careful way, gone.
